castle_page.title: The Castle of Caccamo
castle_page.rhyme_1:
In a Norman castle shaped by time,
come, admire, stop here a while.
It's not just stone, nor a cold rampart,
but an ancient soul awaiting your gaze.
castle_page.history_intro: The Castle was built in 1094 by order of Count Roger I. Over the centuries it passed through 14 noble families — including Chiaramonte, Cabrera and De Spuches — until 1963, when it was handed over to the Sicilian Region.
castle_page.towers: The Torre Mastra, the oldest and tallest, holds a cistern at its base. The Torre Gibellina watches over Terravecchia, while the Torre della Fossa closes off the southern front.
castle_page.size_note: One of the best-preserved Norman castles in Sicily: a full visit takes at least an hour, between courtyards and walkways.
castle_page.biglietti: Tickets — Full price €6 · Reduced online €4.50 · Residents €1 · Students 18-25 €3 · Free under 18.

chiese_page.poesia_intro:
Five temples of stone, of faith and of memory,
open their doors onto a centuries-old story.
chiese_page.poesia_outro: Let yourself be guided where time has stood still...
chiese_page.verse_cappuccini:
At the top, the Capuchins mark where the journey starts,
with an altarpiece and a wide horizon at heart.
chiese_page.verse_angeli:
At the Angels' church, in the most sacred silence, rests
the Blessed Giovanni, the village's own likeness.
chiese_page.verse_annunziata:
Then the Annunziata reveals its painted vaults so fine,
and the bell tower whose watch never declined.
chiese_page.verse_badia:
Further down, the Badia dresses the earth in flower,
with majolica embroidery of rare splendour.
chiese_page.verse_duomo:
Enter the great Duomo, majestic and solemn,
among Gagini's marbles and Stomer's eternal column.

cibo_eventi_page.subtitle: Four seasons, four ways to experience Caccamo
cibo_eventi_page.cta: Ask the Castellana to tell you about it
cibo_eventi_page.s1_body: The Sausage Festival opens the autumn, alongside local sweets like taralli. In December the village lights up with nativity scenes: the Capuchins' one, set up outside the convent with old farming tools and household items from 40-60 years ago, and Santo Domenico's, among the most beautiful to see. Under the Castle the great Christmas tree is lit, and the nearby towns — easily reachable by local transport — often host living nativity scenes.
cibo_eventi_page.s1_tags: Sausage Festival · Capuchins' Nativity Scene · Santo Domenico Nativity Scene · Tree beneath the Castle
cibo_eventi_page.s2_body: The week opens on Palm Sunday with U Signuruzzu a Cavaddu, when a child from the village plays Jesus entering Jerusalem. Good Friday evening brings the living Way of the Cross: the Madonna with the pierced heart meets Christ on a bed of roses. That same day it's customary to "visit the sepulchres" — churches open, altars decked with sprouted wheat, recalling Mary and Magdalene going to Christ's tomb.
cibo_eventi_page.s2_tags: U Signuruzzu a Cavaddu — Palm Sunday · Living Way of the Cross — Good Friday · Visiting the sepulchres · Pane di Cena · Almond lambs
cibo_eventi_page.s3_body: Not just any saint, but a patron entirely Caccamo's own: the Blessed Giovanni Liccio is a son of the village, which is why his feast is among the most heartfelt in the community. The procession crosses the whole town, especially the old quarter — a unique way to see the village in a different light and feel part of the community.
cibo_eventi_page.s3_tags: Patronal procession · Patron saint of Caccamo · Historic centre
cibo_eventi_page.s4_body: Three days of celebration: the historic procession of the Castellana opens the festivities, leading up to the Palio that closes Caccamo's summer.
cibo_eventi_page.s4_tags: Historic procession · Palio · Feast of San Nicasio

canti_page.legend_title: Sister Felicia and the Pomegranate Challenge
canti_page.legend_p1: The majestic Castle of Caccamo, perched on its imposing limestone cliff, holds one of the most fascinating and mysterious stories in all of Sicily: the legend of Sister Felicia, also known as the castle's nun.
canti_page.legend_p2: It is said that Felicia, a girl of extraordinary beauty, was the daughter of the castellan of the time — most likely a nobleman of the Cabrera or Chiaramonte family. As in any proper chivalric drama, the young woman committed the greatest sin for nobility of that era: she fell madly in love with a boy of humble origins, a page or a young soldier of the castle garrison.
canti_page.legend_p3: When the stern father discovered the secret relationship, his reaction was furious. He had the young lover arrested and locked away in the castle's dark dungeons — according to some versions, thrown into one of the infamous "razor wells". To punish his daughter and stifle the scandal, he forced her to take vows, shutting her away for life in an enclosed convent.
canti_page.legend_p4: The girl took the name Sister Felicia. Consumed by grief over her lost love, she died of a broken heart at a young age. But her bond with the castle was too strong to be severed by death: it is said her tormented soul returned there, and still wanders there today.
canti_page.legend_p5: On full-moon nights, right at the stroke of midnight, the nun's ghost appears among the silent halls, dressed in a pure white habit, beautiful and melancholy. In her hands she holds a silver tray bearing a ripe pomegranate, red as blood.
canti_page.legend_p6: If a brave visitor meets her at midnight, she doesn't frighten him: she walks up to him and offers the tray, proposing a challenge. He must shell the pomegranate and eat every single seed, without using his hands and without dropping even one to the ground.
canti_page.legend_p7: If he succeeds, the spell is broken: Sister Felicia points him to the exact spot where an immense treasure lies hidden in the castle's dungeons, before flying up to heaven, finally at peace. If he fails — even by dropping just one seed — the ghost vanishes instantly with a moan of disappointment, leaving the unlucky visitor in the dark.
canti_page.legend_p8: The choice of the pomegranate is no accident: in Mediterranean mythology, it has always been the fruit of the realm of the dead and of unbreakable bonds, as in the Greek myth of Persephone, condemned to remain in the Underworld for eating six pomegranate seeds. In the legend of Sister Felicia, the fruit represents the eternal bond with the afterlife and the broken passion of the two young lovers, sacrificed on the altar of noble pride.
canti_page.legend_p9: To this day, it is said that no one has ever managed to pass the test. Sister Felicia continues to wait, with her silver tray and her pomegranate untouched.

home.poetry:
Beyond the horizon where the lake turns to mirror and glory,
Caccamo weaves its breath into ancient memory.
It's not just stone defying ages and people,
hiding surprising treasures within its walls.

Like a ball of thread slowly unwinding,
it spreads through every alley, every small story.
A weave of centuries revealed with love and mystery,
for those seeking the beating heart of a true village.

Amunì, take the path,
the Castellana is here to keep you company.
